physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's 77.12 degC is a peak temperature for an RL-optimized final placement that is not published, so it cannot be reproduced or numerically compared with a separately generated illustrative placement.

The original thermal evaluation uses HotSpot and an LTI self/mutual-resistance fast model for 2.5D chiplets on an interposer. The interposer, package, heat-spreader and cooling parameters are not given in the paper or pinned config, so the original cooling boundary conditions cannot be matched.

The original method is an RL floorplanner (PPO plus RND) that co-optimizes wirelength and temperature with microbump assignment. A thermal-only Studio run has no optimizer, wirelength or microbump assignment, so that part cannot be replicated.

The paper's workload is a static steady-state power per chiplet, with no transient behaviour, power time series, controller or reliability analysis. Any one-row power trace is a steady-state surrogate only.
The paper's fast thermal model is an LTI approximation with a reported MAE of about 0.25 K vs HotSpot. A different solver will differ in numerical details.
The system is 2.5D (chiplets on an interposer), not 3D stacked, so no vertical stacking mismatch applies. Any Studio 2D model must still represent the interposer layer.
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

studio_assumptions: RLPlanner publishes Ascend910 chiplet sizes and powers, but this config has no placement, power time series, or HotSpot configuration.
The power trace is one constant row made from source per-chiplet watts.
